analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) US Data Review, 2) KRW Update, 3) USDJPY as a Growth Hedge, 4) AI Sell Off & USD and 5) Brazil Equities Upside
key_insights: Fed Chair Warsh, at the IMF meetings, did not address the October FOMC directly but said the world has broadly conformed to the FOMC's September expectations. GS reads this, with other FOMC comments, as a pause in October and still expects a second and final hike in December.

GS estimates September core PCE prices rose 0.34% on the month (0.32% before the PPI report), or +3.12% over the year, after core PPI came in above expectations and the PCE-relevant PPI components were slightly stronger than GS expected.

Core retail sales rose 0.1% in September, below expectations. GS expects consumer spending growth to slow in 2026Q4 as the boost from larger tax refunds fades and higher energy prices remain a headwind.

Business surveys were mixed. The Philadelphia Fed index fell 16.9pt to 20.9 in October, a bigger-than-expected drop in level terms below expectations for a smaller decline, while the Empire index rose 17.9pt to 25.5, well above expectations and the highest since December 2021. GS sees healthy activity but no surge above trend.

GS is more bullish on KRW. A trade surplus above US$40bn a month and high repatriation should keep USDKRW heavy, but the BOK may accumulate reserves at 1300. Governor Shin said KRW at 1330 is still weak versus history and that further appreciation is desirable, so GS sees KRW appreciation below 1300 in the medium term.

GS flow math for Korea: US$30bn a month of exporter USD selling (75% conversion of a US$40bn+ surplus), against about US$7bn FDI+NPS outbound, about US$3bn retail equity outflow and US$5bn NPS hedge buybacks, plus US$2.5bn a month unhedged WGBI inflow until November. That leaves a US$17.5bn monthly surplus before foreign equity flows, and about US$4bn after the US$13bn a month foreign equity outflow seen since July.

GS sees the KOSPI-USDKRW positive correlation weakening because FX hedging of offshore single-name leveraged ETFs is much lower. With US$1.8tn foreign ownership of Korean equities and a 10% average hedge ratio, each 5% KOSPI drop could unwind about US$9bn of hedges, partly offsetting equity outflows. GS expects KRW to keep outperforming TWD in a tech selloff.
GS G10 FX options trading recommends buying USDJPY digital puts (2m 150 strike at 9.55% offer, 6m 144 strike at 9.60% offer, spot ref 157.95) as a growth hedge. Max loss is the premium spent.

GS argues a sell-off in yields has become a bull flattener, which it reads as markets pricing a growth and financing scare rather than only sticky inflation. It cites wider credit spreads across the AI stack, Nasdaq (AI capex demand) and KOSPI (AI capex supply) selling off together, and bull flattening in rates.

Post-CPI FX moves show AI-exposed currencies (USD, KRW, TWD) underperforming while funding currencies (EUR, CHF, JPY) mostly outperform. GS reads this as a terms-of-trade repricing tied to AI capex financing and supply chains rather than classic risk-off.

GS raises the 2022 concept of R**, the rate level above which financial stability and credit concerns start to bite, and says the leveraged AI capex ecosystem may be approaching a yield level where it is materially more rate-sensitive than six months ago.

GS thinks the equities-lower/yields-lower tail is under-hedged by clients, with implied correlation marked near 0% before this week. Hybrid structures have repriced and are now much more expensive, so GS prefers FX vol, which typically outperforms rates vol when recession or credit risks build, with USDJPY vol as its pick.

GS FX Strategy (Kanter) says relative equity performance is what matters for the USD. The DeepSeek episode shifted AI beneficiaries away from the US and was negative for the Dollar, while the February software selloff was less US-specific and did not trigger a 'Dollar down, equities down' episode. The broader equity impulse has shifted from a drag to a support for the Dollar.

GS finds US equity market breadth is among its tightest in decades, and more concentrated rallies coincide with larger Dollar underperformance than equity performance would imply. Rate differentials and terms of trade generally matter more than earnings expectations, as in 2011-2014 when dovish Fed policy weighed on the Dollar despite supportive relative equity performance.

GS EM Strategy says Brazil's Bovespa is up about 8% and MSCI Brazil (EWZ) nearly 15% in USD since the October 4 first-round vote. GS's cyclical macro model attributes about 85% of the Bovespa rally to lower long-end yields (about 150bp decline), and small caps and rate-sensitive stocks are up 15-25%.

Brazil valuations have moved from inexpensive to mid-cycle: MSCI Brazil ex-Commodities was -0.8 s.d. below its 10-year average before the vote and is now near the 12x average, and Bovespa trades at 9.6x NTM P/E versus 9.5x model fair value. Election week saw over $2bn of foreign net buying, but flows remain low versus prior election cycles.

GS keeps its Bovespa target at 215,000 (30%/5% EPS growth in 2026/27, 9.5x target P/E). If 10y local rates fall a further 100-120bp, for a cumulative 290bp since the first round as in 2018, Bovespa could re-rate to 10.1x P/E and reach 225,000. In 2018 Bovespa rose about 15% over six months and small caps and rate-sensitive stocks gained 30-40%.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees scope for further Brazil equity gains if fiscal policy delivers and rates fall, with a possible Bovespa re-rate to 225,000 versus its 215,000 target.

US consumer spending slowdown in 2026Q4 as tax refund support fades and energy prices stay high.
Brazil: rally already reflects much of the rate decline, and further gains depend on actual policy outcomes and implementation.
vol_and_positioning: Implied correlation for the equities-lower/yields-lower scenario was marked at about 0% before this week. Hybrid structures have repriced significantly and are now much more expensive.

GS says FX vol looks attractive versus rates vol for hedging underpriced growth risk premia, because FX vol typically outperforms rates vol when recession or credit risks build. USDJPY vol is the pick.
US equity market breadth is at one of its tightest levels in recent decades after a concentrated rally.
Foreign equity outflow from Korea has averaged US$13bn a month since July. A further 5% KOSPI drop could unwind about US$9bn of RHS FX hedges.
geopolitical: Brazil's first-round election on October 4 raised hopes of a more market-friendly policy outcome, with fiscal policy announcements over coming months a possible upside driver.

tension_points.bull_case: Large trade surplus, high repatriation and BOK Governor Shin's comments that KRW at 1330 is still weak and further appreciation is desirable point to KRW appreciation below 1300 in the medium term.
tension_points.bear_case: The BOK may accumulate reserves at 1300, making it hard for KRW to rally further, and foreign equity outflows of US$13bn a month offset much of the flow surplus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A BOK reserve accumulation line at 1300 that holds, or a steeper KOSPI drop that drives foreign equity outflows beyond the trade-surplus flows.

theme_stances.key_argument: The cost of financing the AI buildout is starting to collide with how much the market can comfortably absorb, seen across credit, equities and rates.
